label: Source kinds
description: Where a citation comes from, in order of preference.

terms.label: Official
terms.description: Publisher or developer, read on their own site (or an archived copy of it, such as the Wayback Machine) or in the game: manual, official site, patch notes, developer posts, in-game text.

terms.label: Established wiki
terms.description: A large, maintained community wiki for the series, including one the developer endorses as its official wiki. A wiki page that copies official text is still a wiki source: say in its note that it copies official text and where the original is.

terms.label: Guide
terms.description: Published strategy guides or long-standing community guides.

terms.label: Video
terms.description: Gameplay footage, cited with a timestamp in the note; official developer videos count as official.

terms.label: Community
terms.description: Forums and discussion threads. Low confidence on their own.

tie_breaks.rule: Code the site you actually read. A wiki page that copies an official profile, manual page or in-game text is wiki, with a note naming the original; confidence still counts the copied text as official. A wiki the developer calls official is still a wiki, because players write it.
